verdicts.verify_by: copy tests/b7-lines-reach-rollout-catalog-featured-pool_test.go into gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/feature/store/ and run go test ./gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/feature/store/ -run TestB7FeaturedCapBehindTrustedNew -v: expect at most 1 trusted among hero+spot, observe 4
verdicts.tldr: The operator cap stays off while 12 trusted apps on New fill the 12-app pool, so the hero and the whole Spotlight show operator apps even after earned apps exist on Top
verdicts.details: eligible() stops at `len(pool) == spotlightPool` (view.go:263) while walking shelves in the realm's order, and homeShelves (front.gno:48-67) sends New first, holding the 16 newest named non-seed apps. featured() then sets `capped := earned >= spotlightSize` from that cut pool. So earned apps on Top are never counted and the cap never applies. The default -trusted-paths (main.go:70) lists 19 namespaces, onbloc and gnoswap among them. Their apps are not seeds, so `core` stays false and they land on New: 12 trusted apps on New is a realistic launch state, not a made-up input. The doc's promise that operator apps take 'one place at most' once spotlightSize apps have earned theirs does not hold, and the comment at view.go:249 ('shelf order, which puts quality first') is wrong, since New is ordered by age. Fix: build the pool from every shelf before cutting it, or count earned over all eligible apps, and cut to spotlightPool only after ranking by quality (Top and Trending ahead of New).

'day 3: hero+spot=[t04 t10 t11 t12] trusted=4', --- FAIL. Input: 12 tierTrusted apps on shelf 1 (New), 4 tierRegistered Earned apps on shelf 2 (Top). Base 47d19f8a3: gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/feature/store and r/gnoland/store do not exist (ls: No such file or directory), so the PR adds the feature.

verdicts.verify_by: go test ./gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/feature/store/ -run TestB7TrendingHeroBehindTrustedNew -v with the same repro file: expect hero=hot, observe hero=t01
verdicts.tldr: When New already carries 12 eligible apps, the week's top eligible app is never the hero, and the page shows the daily rotation labelled 'In the spotlight today' instead
verdicts.details: trending() accepts a candidate only if `slices.Contains(pool, l)` (view.go:338), and pool is the first 12 eligible apps in shelf order, New first. An earned app is at least earnAge old (listing.gno:689), so on an active chain it has usually left New's 16-newest window. If New holds 12 eligible apps (trusted, or earned on a quiet chain), the leader of the trending shelf is outside the pool. featured() then falls through to `pool[day%len(pool)]` with labelRotation. That breaks the documented 'else the eligible app with the most momentum this week'. Eligibility is a property of the app, and pool membership is not the right test for it. Fix: in trending(), test `l.Kind == kindApp && l.tier.rich(l.Earned)` instead of pool membership, or build the pool over every shelf as for #22.

verdicts.verify_by: copy tests/b7-lines-reach-rollout-catalog-stale-moment_test.gno into examples/gno.land/r/gnoland/store/v0/ and run cd examples && gno test ./gno.land/r/gnoland/store/v0 -run TestB7StaleSeedMoment -v (passes: same seed activity a year later), then tests/b7-lines-reach-rollout-catalog-stale-moment_test.go in the gnoweb store package with -run TestB7MomentHasNoAge
verdicts.tldr: On an idle store the pulse keeps saying a seed app 'just joined' long after deploy, because activity events carry no height
verdicts.details: event in pulse.gno:20-24 holds only Kind, Listing and Stars, with no height. The ring (pulse.gno:26-49) holds events until 20 newer ones push them out. writeActivity (api.gno:182-191) serves the newest 5 with no age, and latestMoment always writes `l.Title + " just joined"` for a 'listed' event. The seed's init upserts the core apps, which are tracked as 'listed', so right after deploy and on any later idle stretch the pulse reads 'Valopers just joined' next to the current block. That includes a seed app that never 'joined' at all. The text corrects itself at the next listing, update or milestone, and the worst case is stale copy, so this is banded Nit, not Warning. Fix: record the height in event and serve it, and have latestMoment drop or re-phrase an event older than a window (e.g. a week of blocksPerDay); or leave seed events out of the activity feed.
